classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught squared-denominator method, factor quadratic or cubic products, interpret repeated factors and exclude original denominator zeros.

answer.worked:
Multiply both sides by $(2x-1)^2$, which is positive for $x\ne\frac12$.
$$\begin{aligned}5x(2x-1)&\ge 3(2x-1)^2\\5x(2x-1)-3(2x-1)^2&\ge 0\\(2x-1)(3-x)&\ge 0\end{aligned}$$
The product is non-negative for $\frac12\le x\le3$. Exclude $x=\frac12$, where the original denominator is zero.
$$\frac12<x\le3$$

Multiply both sides by $(x+4)^2$, which is positive for $x\ne-4$.
$$\begin{aligned}(2x-3)(x+4)&\le(x+4)^2\\(2x-3)(x+4)-(x+4)^2&\le0\\(x+4)(x-7)&\le0\end{aligned}$$
The product is non-positive for $-4\le x\le7$. Exclude $x=-4$.
$$-4<x\le7$$

Multiply both sides by $(x+3)^2$, which is positive for $x\ne-3$.
$$\begin{aligned}(2x+5)(x+3)&<(x+3)^2\\(2x+5)(x+3)-(x+3)^2&<0\\(x+3)(x+2)&<0\end{aligned}$$
The product is negative between its roots. The restriction $x\ne-3$ is already satisfied.
$$-3<x<-2$$

Multiply both sides by $(x+1)^2$, which is positive for $x\ne-1$.
$$\begin{aligned}x(x+3)(x+1)&<2(x+1)^2\\(x+1)\bigl(x(x+3)-2(x+1)\bigr)&<0\\(x+1)(x^2+x-2)&<0\\(x+1)(x+2)(x-1)&<0\end{aligned}$$
The cubic has roots $-2,-1,1$ and positive leading coefficient. It is negative for $x<-2$ and $-1<x<1$. These intervals satisfy $x\ne-1$.
$$x<-2\quad\text{or}\quad-1<x<1$$

Multiply both sides by $(x-2)^2$, which is positive for $x\ne2$.
$$\begin{aligned}(x^2-4)(x-2)&>0\\(x-2)^2(x+2)&>0\end{aligned}$$
For $x\ne2$, the squared factor is positive, so the product is positive when $x+2>0$. Retain the original restriction.
$$x>-2,\qquad x\ne2$$

Multiply both sides by $(x-3)^2$, which is positive for $x\ne3$.
$$\begin{aligned}4(x-3)&\le x(x-3)^2\\x(x-3)^2-4(x-3)&\ge0\\(x-3)(x^2-3x-4)&\ge0\\(x-3)(x-4)(x+1)&\ge0\end{aligned}$$
The cubic has roots $-1,3,4$ and positive leading coefficient. It is non-negative on $[-1,3]$ and $[4,\infty)$. Exclude $x=3$.
$$-1\le x<3\quad\text{or}\quad x\ge4$$

The restrictions are $x\ne0,-2$. Multiply both sides by $x^2(x+2)^2$, which is positive on this domain.
$$\begin{aligned}x(x+2)^2&\le x^2(x+2)\\x(x+2)^2-x^2(x+2)&\le0\\2x(x+2)&\le0\end{aligned}$$
The product is non-positive for $-2\le x\le0$. Both endpoints make an original denominator zero, so exclude them.
$$-2<x<0$$

Multiply both sides by $x^2$, which is positive for $x\ne0$.
$$\begin{aligned}x^3+x&\ge2x^2\\x^3-2x^2+x&\ge0\\x(x-1)^2&\ge0\end{aligned}$$
For $x<0$, the product is negative. For $x>0$, it is non-negative, including equality at $x=1$. Exclude $x=0$.
$$x>0$$
